options: Planning, putting the plan into action, and measuring progress and performance
questions.explain: Planning, executing and monitoring repeat throughout the project.
questions.evidence: Project management is a process that includes planning, putting the project plan into action, and measuring progress and performance.

questions.q: In the project life cycle, which two questions do feasibility and justification answer?
options: Can we do the project? Should we do the project?
When does it end? How long will it take?
questions.explain: A feasibility study compares options before a project is initiated.
questions.evidence: Issues of feasibility (“can we do the project?”) and justification (“should we do the project?”) are addressed.

questions.q: Who decides whether a project is worth undertaking and will be profitable for the organisation?
questions.explain: The sponsor owns the business case.
questions.evidence: It is up to the project sponsor to determine if the project is worth undertaking and whether the project will be profitable to the organization.

questions.q: How is a project's return on investment (ROI) calculated?
options: Benefits divided by the number of team members
Benefits minus costs, divided by costs
Total costs divided by the project's duration
questions.explain: ROI expresses the net gain relative to what was invested.
questions.evidence: This is calculated by subtracting the project’s costs from the benefits and then dividing by the costs.

options: Tangible outcomes, measurable results or specific items that must be produced to complete the project or phase
questions.explain: Describe each deliverable in enough detail to tell it apart from related ones.
questions.evidence: Project deliverables are tangible outcomes, measurable results, or specific items that must be produced to consider either the project or the project phase completed.

questions.q: How does a requirements traceability matrix help?
options: It assigns tasks to team members
It links each requirement to business and project objectives so it adds business value
questions.explain: It also tracks requirements through the life cycle so approved ones are delivered.
questions.evidence: The implementation of a requirements traceability matrix helps ensure that each requirement adds business value by linking it to the business and project objectives.

options: Because the first activity's finish leads into the second activity's start
Because the project starts when it finishes
Because the second task must finish first
questions.explain: It is the most common dependency type in network diagrams.
questions.evidence: It’s called finish-to-start because the first activity’s finish leads into the second activity’s start

questions.q: In earned value management, what is the planned value (PV)?
options: The value of the work actually completed
The amount of work that should have been done by a particular date
The budget left at the end
questions.explain: Comparing PV, earned value and actual cost shows schedule and cost performance.
questions.evidence: The amount of work that should have been done by a particular date is the planned value (PV)

questions.q: When is accepting a risk your only choice?
options: When the risk is very likely
When you can't avoid it and nothing can reduce its impact
questions.explain: Other responses are to avoid, mitigate or transfer the risk.
questions.evidence: If you can’t avoid the risk, and there’s nothing you can do to reduce its impact, then accepting it is your only choice.

options: A way of visualising and improving current working practices so work flows quickly
questions.explain: Smooth flow delivers value quickly and gets early feedback.
questions.evidence: Kanban is a way of visualising and improving your current working practices so that work flows through a system quickly.

questions.q: How does the Scrum Guide define Scrum?
options: A lightweight framework that helps people, teams and organisations generate value through adaptive solutions for complex problems
A detailed method that prescribes every task
questions.explain: Scrum is deliberately incomplete, defining only what is required.
questions.evidence: Scrum is a lightweight framework that helps people, teams and organizations generate value through adaptive solutions for complex problems.

questions.q: What is the most important part of a user story?
questions.explain: Stories briefly explain the actor, the narrative and — most importantly — the goal.
questions.evidence: The most important part of a user story is the goal.
